subject: medicine
title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

steps.tx: Ask about **smoking history** with pack years and biomass fuel exposure, because most Indian COPD follows tobacco or chulha smoke. Clarify **progressive breathlessness** that is persistent and worsens with exertion over years, with winter exacerbations needing admission. Note **sputum pattern** with morning mucoid expectoration that turns purulent during flares, plus weight loss, cor pulmonale swelling, early onset disease suggesting alpha-1 deficiency, and past tuberculosis with destroyed lung. Grade disability with the mMRC scale.
steps.say: Take a smoking history with pack years and ask about chulha smoke because both strongly predict COPD. Establish that breathlessness is persistent and progressive over years and worsens on exertion. Ask about morning sputum and note when it becomes purulent during winter exacerbations. Check weight loss and ankle swelling because cachexia and cor pulmonale mark advanced disease. You should ask about early onset disease with family history and past tuberculosis because both change the differential.

steps.tx: Look for **barrel chest** with increased anteroposterior diameter and horizontal ribs from hyperinflation. Watch **accessory muscles** working with scalene contraction and pursed lip breathing during expiration. Note quiet breath sounds with wheeze and hyperresonant percussion from trapped air. Examine for **cor pulmonale** with raised jugular pressure and ankle oedema, plus temporalis wasting from cachexia. Remember that clubbing is unusual in pure COPD and should prompt a search for bronchiectasis or malignancy. Check oximetry and body mass.
steps.say: Inspect the chest for hyperinflation with increased anteroposterior diameter and horizontal ribs. Watch the neck muscles working and observe pursed lip breathing during expiration. Percuss for hyperresonance and listen for quiet breath sounds with wheeze from trapped air. Look for raised jugular pressure and ankle oedema because these signs indicate cor pulmonale. Remember that clubbing is unusual in pure COPD, so search for bronchiectasis or malignancy when you find it.

steps.tx: Study the photograph for **barrel chest** with a hyperinflated thorax that reflects chronic air trapping and flattened diaphragms. Notice **pursed lip breathing** with a close up inset, which prolongs expiration and relieves breathlessness, plus visible neck muscle recruitment during inspiration. Link these signs to quiet breath sounds and hyperresonance on examination, and remember that such hyperinflation predicts exertional limitation. Use the image in exams to describe findings in order from inspection to palpation and auscultation.
steps.say: Look at the photograph and note the hyperinflated barrel shaped thorax from chronic air trapping. Observe the neck muscles working during inspiration and the pursed lips that prolong expiration. Link these inspection signs to quiet breath sounds and hyperresonance on examination. Mention flattened diaphragms and exertional limitation when you present the case because examiners reward a linked description.

steps.tx: Confirm obstruction with **post bronchodilator spirometry** showing FEV1 over FVC below 0.70, then stage airflow limitation with GOLD grades 1 to 4. Assess symptoms and exacerbation history to assign groups A, B or E and guide inhaled therapy. Review **chest imaging** with hyperinflated lungs and flat diaphragms on radiograph, and use CT to confirm emphysema or exclude bronchiectasis. Check arterial gases for retained carbon dioxide, echocardiography for pulmonary hypertension, alpha-1 levels in early disease, and sputum culture during purulent flares. Score **BODE index** to predict admissions and mortality.
steps.say: Confirm obstruction when post bronchodilator FEV1 over FVC falls below 0.70 on spirometry. Stage airflow limitation with GOLD grades and combine symptoms with exacerbation history to assign groups A, B or E. Review the radiograph for hyperinflation with flat diaphragms and use CT to confirm emphysema or exclude bronchiectasis. Check arterial gases for retained carbon dioxide and request echocardiography when pulmonary hypertension is suspected. Send sputum culture during purulent flares and calculate the BODE score because it predicts admissions and mortality.

vis.alt: COPD staging: post-bronchodilator FEV1 over FVC below 0.70 confirms obstruction; GOLD 1 at 80 percent predicted or above, GOLD 2 from 50 to 79, GOLD 3 from 30 to 49, GOLD 4 below 30; groups A, B and E combine symptoms with exacerbation history; BODE scores BMI, obstruction, dyspnoea and exercise from 0 to 10.
vis.caption: Grade the blockage, group the burden, BODE the road ahead.

steps.tx: Start with **smoking cessation** because quitting is the single best step to slow decline, with yearly vaccines for cover. Build **inhaled therapy** around a long acting antimuscarinic, adding a long acting beta agonist and inhaled steroid when eosinophils or frequent flares justify it. Treat **exacerbation plan** with short steroids and antibiotics for purulent change, using controlled oxygen at 88 to 92 percent and noninvasive ventilation for acidosis. Offer pulmonary rehabilitation, consider long term oxygen for 15 hours daily in chronic hypoxia, and select a few patients for valves or transplant.
steps.say: Help every patient quit smoking because cessation slows decline more than any drug. Build inhaled therapy around a long acting antimuscarinic and step up when flares persist. Give yearly vaccines and enrol the patient in pulmonary rehabilitation to improve exercise capacity. Treat flares with short steroids and antibiotics when sputum turns purulent, keeping oxygen between 88 and 92 percent. Use noninvasive ventilation for acidosis and consider long term oxygen or referral for valves and transplant in selected cases.
